clue.text: Poet having rare delicacy on part of Hebridean island

indicators.note: rare here means unusual or out of the ordinary, so the word beside it is to be taken in an unusual order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
Lewis and Harris is one Outer Hebridean island; Lewis is its northern part

explanation.surface: A poet savouring an uncommon delicacy while visiting a remote Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the island after the reworked delicacy. Cecil Day-Lewis was Poet Laureate from 1968 to 1972.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Day-Lewis was an Anglo-Irish writer of verse and a former UK Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Musical, elegant with a vitality

parts.note: chic means stylish or elegant
taken as written
go means energy or vitality

explanation.surface: A review praising a stage show as stylish and full of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a Kander and Ebb stage show about jazz-age murderesses, so it is a well-known example.

clue.text: Found, ornate mace and a crucifix

indicators.note: ornate suggests something elaborately worked over, so the words that follow are reworked into new order

parts.note: the first part of the fodder, as written
the rest of the fodder, as written
a crucifix is a cross bearing the figure of Christ

explanation.surface: An inventory of church treasures turned up: a decorated ceremonial mace and a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' sits inside the anagram's run of words but is only a joiner: the fodder is just mace plus a.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across something is to find it by chance, a phrasal-verb synonym of discovered.

clue.text: One may be asked by counsel in prominent matter

definitions.text: One may be asked by counsel

parts.note: leading means foremost or prominent
a matter under discussion is a question, as in 'the question of funding'

explanation.surface: A lawyer in a high-profile case puts something to a witness.
explanation.definitionFit: In court, an advocate's query that prompts the desired reply is one barristers are restricted from putting to their own witness.

clue.text: At each stage from A to B on the London Underground?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: throughout, at every point

definitions.text: from A to B on the London Underground
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: making the whole journey on one Tube route

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a whimsical literal reading of the idiom, as if travelling every station of a Tube route.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at every point or in every respect, and literally it describes covering a whole railway route.

clue.text: Girl, awfully ill close to infirmary

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the word after it comes out jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, as written

indicators.note: close here means the end, so only the final letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the end of infirmary

explanation.surface: A very sick young woman is near the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily is a female first name, and crosswords often define names simply as girl.

clue.text: US city with CIA involvement

indicators.note: involvement suggests things entangled together, so the letters are mixed in with one another

parts.note: part of the fodder, as written
the rest of the fodder, as written

explanation.surface: A news item about an American town where the intelligence agency has a hand in things.
explanation.definitionFit: Wichita is the largest city in Kansas, an example of an American city.

clue.text: Girl uses an eccentric knight inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the knight goes within the reworked letters
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the words before it are rearranged oddly

parts.note: the fodder, as written
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A young woman makes use of an odd chivalrous admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight is N, as in chess notation, since K is already the king; it sits between the A and the final NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Susanne is a female first name, which crosswords commonly define as girl.

clue.text: Racing driver frustrated in a fog

indicators.note: frustrated means thwarted or upset, so the words after it are knocked out of order

parts.note: the fodder, as written

explanation.surface: A motorsport star is held up because he cannot see in murky conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan Manuel Fangio was an Argentine Formula One champion who won five world titles in the 1950s.

clue.text: Self-evident truth adult associate recalled about love

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the associate-plus-love unit is read from the end
about means surrounding, so the word for associate goes around the love symbol

parts.note: to mix is to associate or socialise
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A grown-up's colleague remembered some obvious truth about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes just after the first letter of MIX, and that unit is then turned round and placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as true without proof, a self-evident principle.

clue.text: Team everybody boycotts

parts.note: all means everybody
to black something is to boycott it, as unions blacked goods in a dispute

explanation.surface: A squad that everyone refuses to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: To black, in British trade-union usage, is to refuse to handle goods or work during a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: The All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby union side, so the name denotes a sports team.

clue.text: Fruit that could make one unwell in old Moorish city

indicators.note: in says the word for unwell is placed within the city's name

parts.note: Granada in Andalusia was the last Moorish kingdom in Spain
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A warning about some exotic produce from Spain that might give you a stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for unwell slips in just before the city's last letter. The surface's 'one unwell' is only padding for the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The granadilla is a passion fruit, a tropical fruit of the passionflower vine.

clue.text: Appellation belonging to Dallaglio, naturally?

indicators.note: belonging to says the letters are owned by, so lie within, the following words

parts.note: found across the end of the surname and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A nickname that a famous rugby player would obviously have.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence Dallaglio, an England rugby forward, toured with the British and Irish Lions, so the whole clue also defines the title he earned.
explanation.definitionFit: Players picked for the British and Irish Lions rugby tour are each called a Lion, a title Dallaglio held.

clue.text: Managed to explain note after Territorial Army dance

indicators.note: after says the reserve-army abbreviation is placed first, with the other pieces following it

parts.note: TA is the abbreviation for the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
ran means managed, as in ran a business
to tell can mean to explain or make known
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in writing a memo following a reserve-forces dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after Territorial Army' tells us TA comes first, before the managed, explain and note pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a lively Italian folk dance, traditionally linked to tarantula bites.

clue.text: Distinctive smell of European river, some say

indicators.note: some say points to how the word is spoken by some people, not how it is spelt

parts.note: the Oder forms part of the border between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: A characteristic whiff coming off a continental waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the river and the smell sound much alike, which is why it is hedged as only some say.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent or smell, often a characteristic one.

clue.text: Gaudy public house, good in Winter, say

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written
the Winter Palace in St Petersburg is one example of a palace

explanation.surface: A showy pub that is pleasant to visit in the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winter, say' gives an example of a type of building: the Winter Palace was the Russian tsars' residence.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin palace was a flashily decorated Victorian pub, and the phrase still means an ornate bar.

clue.text: Formal wear in smooth clubs, perhaps

parts.note: to dress stone or timber is to smooth and finish its surface
clubs is one of the four suits of cards

explanation.surface: Evening attire worn at slick nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress suit is a man's evening suit with tails, worn on formal occasions.

clue.text: Radical doctor with a short cane

indicators.note: short says the word is cut back, losing its final letter

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: An extreme medic carries a little walking cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic and radical both describe sweeping, far-reaching action.

clue.text: All together in new manse on outskirts of Stoke

indicators.note: new suggests the word after it is remade into a fresh order

parts.note: the fodder, as written; a manse is a minister's house

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters of the town are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Stoke

explanation.surface: A congregation all crammed into a newly built minister's house at the edge of a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the outer letters of Stoke after the reworked manse. Stoke-on-Trent is a city in Staffordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French for 'in a body', meaning everyone together as a group.

clue.text: Accumulate a large number

parts.note: taken as written
a mass is a large quantity or crowd

explanation.surface: An instruction to gather up plenty of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one plain phrase, but only the first word defines; the rest builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or pile up over time, a direct synonym of accumulate.

clue.text: Notice one model is fat

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
I is the Roman numeral for one
to pose is to model for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: Pointing out that a particular model is overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means fatty, as in adipose tissue, the body's fat-storing layer.

clue.text: Nurse in obstetrics is terrific

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A maternity-ward carer is excellent at her job.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a senior British hospital nurse, so the two words are interchangeable as ward titles.

clue.text: Girl about right for service

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the name goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a female first name
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A young woman who is suitable for national service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' here means one of the armed forces, not help given.
explanation.definitionFit: The army is one of the armed services, alongside the navy and air force.

clue.text: Discovers fool swallowing some

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the word for fool goes around the other piece

parts.note: an ass is a fool
certain means some, as in certain people

explanation.surface: An idiot finds out by eating a bit of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for sure, so ascertains matches discovers as a third-person verb.

clue.text: Pretty fine tune

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an air is a melody or tune

explanation.surface: A rather good melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty fine' reads as 'quite good', but pretty is the definition and fine is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair, in an old-fashioned sense, means beautiful or good-looking, as in a fair maiden.

clue.text: Conductor of opera one located in pub on the way back

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the pub unit reads backwards
located in says the numeral sits within the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A conductor of an opera found in a pub on his way home.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral sits between the pub's two Ns before that unit turns round. Tosca is Puccini's opera about a singer in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral and opera conductor.

clue.text: Ring worn by miss, unattached

indicators.note: something worn by a person is on them, wrapped round by them, so the ring goes inside

parts.note: to miss a chance is to lose it
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A young woman without a partner is wearing a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like the title for an unmarried woman, which fits 'unattached', but it is the verb meaning lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means free or not fastened, so it can replace unattached.

clue.text: Everything must go here

parts.note: surface reading: a command that everything should be put in one place
setter's reading: the slogan on a shop's banner when it is selling off all its stock

explanation.surface: Someone ordering all the belongings to be piled in one spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everything must go' is the familiar shop-window slogan of a sale where all stock is sold off cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop holding a closing-down sell-off advertises that everything must go, so the slogan describes that event.
